complete_units.complete_normalized_historical_latin: 〈I.4〉 〈De natura VII stellarum mobilium〉 〈S〉olis naturam apud omnes calidam et siccam constat esse, moderate tamen. Huius equidem effectus tanto altior atque dignior, quanto ceterarum actionibus stellarum eminentior pro sui corporis magnitudine reperitur. Unde etiam temporis mutationem sibi attribuunt. Hic quanto vertici nostre vicinius accedit, eo amplius multiplices apud nos calores efficit. Luna autem in maxima parte humida. Circulus enim suus terre vicinior multoque ex ea suscepto 〈vapore〉 quedam corpora conficit vetustate, alia corrumpit putretudine. Cum autem Soli opposita fuerit, ex proprio quem retinet calore quibusdam prestat maturitate, modum tamen in nullo transcendens. Ipsa namque lumen a Sole capit. In Saturni natura frigus et siccitas redundant. Circulus enim illius a calore Solis alienus frigus contrahit, ab humore autem quem terre vapor generat remotus siccitatem recipit. Habent etiam isti et alii planete secundum locorum distantiam a Sole in hoc nostro circulo non modicam virtutis efficaciam, eorum mutatio varietatis secundum naturarum diversitatem et secundum propriam ipsius substantie operationem in augmento sive diminutione patescit. Est etiam in accessu sive recessu earumdem ad invicem alia variatio. Martis autem natura comburens et sicca. Color enim igneus et ipse Soli vicinus, cui circulus secundo loco ab eo ordinatur. In Iovis natura equalitas conveniensque temperantia precellit. Illius namque circulus inter duos circulos, Saturni scilicet et Martis, constitutus et ipse Iupiter inter utramque naturam, calidam videlicet et frigidam, non minus ordinatur, eiusque propria et principalis virtus calor, semper fomentum ministrans. Hec itaque causa ventos excitat quorum flatus beneficio arbores pullulant et plante virescunt. Veneris autem moderata compositio et virtus equabilis Solis, tamen affinitate non nimium calescit. Preterea, quoniam multa luce refulget, humorem a terre vapore[m] concretum in se recipit. Unde et ipsa, sicut et Luna, humectat. Mercurius quoque, quoniam cursus eius in longitudine semper Soli proximus, quandoque calescit, lunari quidem circulo totam terram obeunti factus vicinior invicem humectat. Est etiam in causa sui cursus celeritas levitasque revolutionis alternaque circa Solem frequensque mutatio. Unde subtilis et calidus effectus variationi aut alterationi sepius non repugnat.

complete_units.complete_normalized_historical_latin: 〈I.5〉 〈De fortuna et infortunio stellarum〉 〈H〉iis de natura stellarum et de virtutis moderatione prelibatis de fortuna et infortunio earumdem consequenter dicemus. Quatuor enim nature sive potius virtutes que mundanorum omnium efficientes cause recte dici possunt, quar〈um〉 due, calor videlicet et humor, arboribus incrementum, herbis et plantis quemdam vegetandi motum, animantibus etiam vitam conferunt, frigus autem et siccitas econtra dissipant, corrumpunt, dispergunt. Hoc equidem modo stellarum mobilium due, Iupiter videlicet et Venus, equabiles concordisque sunt moderationis. Ab hiis etiam Luna non videtur differre. Hac igitur consideratione philosophi veteres illas fortuitas et in melius omnia revocantes pro supradicta earum oportunitate dixerunt. Harum namque virtus in calore et humore precipue subsistit. Saturni autem et Martis efficacia predictis tribus adversatur, quoniam harum duarum nature diversitas illarum trium naturam non respicit, quare altera frigus, altera sibi proprie siccitatem usurpat. Unde, quoniam in natura constantiam non amittunt, infortunate facte sunt. Sol denique et Mercurius ad omnes se inclinant, nunc hinc, nunc inde se invicem divertentes. Hoc autem in hiis satis possibile videtur, quoniam in earum natura participatio quedam continetur.

complete_units.complete_normalized_historical_latin: 〈I.6〉 〈Que sint mascule, que muliebres〉 In primordio humane creationis, quoniam in natura sive potius in sexu duo tantum conditi reperiuntur, masculus scilicet et femina, naturam 〈caloris sexui masculino, naturam〉 humoris sexui feminino attribuunt, quare altera in alterum iuste concessit participatio. Cum in Luna et in Venere maximus humor habundet, has antiqui femineas appellarunt. 〈Solem quidem et Saturnum, Iovem similiter et Martem contrario sexui reli〈n〉querunt〉. Mercurius quoque, quoniam utriusque generis particeps extitit, in moderatione caloris et humoris equalitatem non amisit. Nec minus etiam secundum earum mansiones a Sole sexus rationem exponunt. Cum enim planete orientales ortum videlicet Solis precedunt, masculino sexui ascribuntur. Cum autem ab occidente solarem occasum premiserunt, femineum sortiuntur. Preterea, prout earum mansiones ab orizonte distiterint, idem coniciunt. Si itaque ab oriente inter medium celum superius et orizonta disponantur, aut si ab occidentis partibus inter orizonta et medium celum inferius, quod cardo terre dicitur, locum obtineant, sexum virilem assumunt; quod si in reliquis quartis exstiterint, femineum non relinquunt.

complete_units.complete_normalized_historical_latin: 〈I.7〉 〈Que diurne, que nocturne〉 〈D〉uo esse tempora omnes nullo rationis induti argumento, verum cotidiano docti experimento fateri coguntur. Alterum dicitur dies et hunc masculis, alterum vocatur nox et hanc mulieribus attribuunt. Cum igitur in die pro motu et variatione mundanorum, sed precipue pro munero scolarium exercitio negotiorum maxime calor habundet, in nocte quidem omnia quiete fruuntur, cum a labore omnia cessent animantia et tunc humor etiam prevaleat, Lunam et Venerem nocturnas dixerunt, Solem et Iovem diurnas vocantes. Mercurium quoque, quia utriusque est particeps, inter utramque medium reli〈n〉querunt. Sed cum orientalis fuerit, diurnus, cum autem occidentalis, nocturnus dicetur. Duas itaque infortunatas, quas etiam corruptionis ministras appellant, a sue nature convenientia removentes in contrarium collocarunt. Mars namque, quotiens in melius revocatur, profectus suos in meliora multiplicat; in sui natura persistens, infortunium in deterius redundat. Saturnus ergo pro expressa ipsius frigiditate diurnus vocatur. Illius etenim naturam diei calor mitigat. Mars autem nocturnus ponitur, quoniam ipsius siccitatem noctis humor temperat. Eodemque denique modo in omnibus infortunatis. Cum enim in contrarium se applicant vel divertunt, eorum minuitur infortunium, dum earum roboratur moderatio.

complete_units.complete_normalized_historical_latin: 〈I.8〉 〈De virtute stellarum secundum locorum diversitates et earum mansiones a Sole〉 〈L〉una equidem et stelle nocturne in augmento sive diminutione secundum loca earum 〈et〉 mansiones a Sole vires suas permutare creduntur. A primo namque ipsius Lune exortu donec atharbe primum occupet, quod medium prioris lucis dicitur, in ipsius lunaris corporis natura humor videtur prevalere. A medio item prioris lucis quousque Soli opponatur, calor dicitur preesse. Ab ipso quidem totius lucis complemento donec atharbe secundum insideat, quod medium secunde lucis nominant, regnat siccitas. A medio demum secunde lucis quousque Soli iungatur, viget frigiditas. Erratice igitur stelle a sui ortus primordio quousque moram primam consequa〈n〉tur, humectant. Ab eo quidem loco quousque ad Solis oppositionem ventum fuerit, calescunt; a Solis rursum oppositione donec secundam moram obtineant, desiccant. Cum autem hic locus relinquatur quousque Solem succedant, frigescunt. Diversa namque vis earum naturalisque moderatio, preterea quia in hoc circulo altera alteri quasi victrix prefertur secundum earum mansiones et loca huius rei cognitionem insinuant. Ex hoc demum, quod in circulo per diversitatem sive potius rerum alterationem recensetur, quod dictum est nobis manifestius innotuit.

I.4: Sun: moderate heat/dryness, magnitude and seasonal action; nearer our zenith gives us more heat.

Moon: mainly moisture, near Earth and receives vapour; bodily ageing/putrefaction wording remains uncertain in interpretation; opposition to Sun linked to moderate own warmth and maturitate, with nativitatem V1 variant; receives light from Sun.
Saturn: cold/dry, remote from solar heat and terrestrial vapour.
All planets: solar distance and mutual approach/recession qualify powers.
Mars: burning/dry, reddish and near Sun in the stated order.
Jupiter: tempered between Saturn/Mars, warmth and favourable winds, trees/plants grow.
Venus: moderate near Sun; bright, receives terrestrial vapour and moistens like Moon.
Mercury: alternating warming near Sun and moistening near lunar circuit, variable rapid course.
I.5: Heat/moisture support plant growth and animal life; cold/dry corrupt in this attributed account.
Sun/Mercury can incline either way; no context-free benefic label.
I.6: Heat/masculine and moisture/feminine classifications are historical sex analogies.
Moon/Venus feminine; Sun/Saturn/Jupiter/Mars masculine in editorial supplement; Mercury mixed.
Oriental/western relation to Sun changes classification.
Horizon quadrants also change classification; no human genital/anatomical observation.
I.7: Day/night distinguished, historically compared with male/female.
Day has abundant heat with activity; night has moisture with animal rest.
Moon/Venus nocturnal, Sun/Jupiter diurnal; Mercury intermediate, oriental=diurnal/western=nocturnal.
Malefics assigned contrary context: Saturn own coldness moderated by daytime heat; Mars own dryness tempered by nighttime moisture.
Mars improved disposition increases favourable results, own nature worsens misfortune; contrary application reduces misfortune as moderation strengthens.
I.8: Moon/nocturnal-star powers change with solar-relative positions.
Moon first appearance→first atharbe/half-prior-light: moisture predominates; that point→solar opposition: heat.
Complete light→second atharbe/half-second-light: dryness; then→solar conjunction: coldness.
Wandering stars first rise→first station: moisten; then→opposition: warm; then→second station: dry; then followingSun: cool.
Intrinsic force and moderation combined with location and predominance; no fixed day counts or recipe protocol.

prospective_minimal_hypothesis.construction: DECLARE_R(R,q); QUALIFY_C(C,p); MODERATE(R,q,C,p) -> E(R,C,qualifiedPower); CONSEQUENCE(E,R) -> attributed reduced harm. Require two written instances sharing the operator but using cold/heat and dry/moisture pairs.
prospective_minimal_hypothesis.relational_obligation: RecipientID in intrinsic property, moderation and downstream consequence must be identical. Context and its opposing quality must be written or obtained by one fixed declared reference rule. Output is qualified power, not a new Quality name or Boolean negation.
prospective_minimal_hypothesis.smallest_scope: One already admitted complete unit containing two different typed inputs and their consequence, full three-reader raw scope; coordinator selects unit later. No target unit acquired here.
prospective_minimal_hypothesis.target_binding_requirement: A complete authored target construction must bind the recipient-owned quality, opposing-context argument and effect/result consumer from literal source groups; no merely ambient illness/quality or Sun/Moon names and no omitted uncertain controls.
prospective_minimal_hypothesis.cost_if_authored: Price any new whole/part meanings, nominal frames, oppositional relation, context scope, reference resolver, output type and consequence rule. No inherited ar/aiin/qo meaning is confirmed.
prospective_minimal_hypothesis.distinguishing_countercase: Unary OPPOSITE returns only Quality and cannot supply E(R,C). A merely negated effective quality does not express the source-specified contextual moderation and consequence; same-state q/NOT(q) collisions must be assessed only after assigning the same property frame. Baseline and qualified effect cannot be collapsed to manufacture a contradiction. Pure intervals/names lack recipient-indexed effect.
prospective_minimal_hypothesis.falsifier: Under a fixed complete target grammar, if alleged result is an interval/name/quality rather than recipient-indexed qualified power, if same R cannot be retained, if opposed context comes only from guessed picture/ambient state, or if downstream consequence lacks its output argument, this specific construction fails or remains UNKNOWN. Do not repair with new nouns/context after applications.
prospective_minimal_hypothesis.scope_boundary: No global decoder, per-whole lookup, anonymous graph retrieval or reserve use. Source scaffold is possibility, not target translation confirmation.
prospective_minimal_hypothesis.baseline_effect_separation: Baseline profile is a reference/description used as an input; qualifiedPower is a context-indexed attributed result. This does not assert the physical quality remains numerically unchanged after moderation or that baseline q and NOT(q) hold in the same effective state.
